questions.question: What is the standard way to run one test suite on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit?
options: Copy the spec files into one folder per browser
Read an environment variable inside each test
Define one project per browser in `playwright.config.ts`
Launch each browser by hand in a `beforeAll` hook
questions.explanation: Each project applies its own `use` settings to the same test files, so nothing is duplicated.

questions.question: A WebKit project sets `userAgent` to a Firefox user agent string. Which engine renders the page?
options: WebKit
Firefox
Chromium
Whichever engine matches the user agent
questions.explanation: `userAgent` only changes the string the browser reports. The engine stays the same.

questions.question: The config sets `permissions: ['clipboard-read']` at the top level. What happens in the Firefox project?
options: Firefox shows a permission prompt
Tests fail with an `Unknown permission` error
The permission is ignored and tests carry on
Playwright switches that project to Chromium
questions.explanation: Firefox accepts only a few permission names and throws on the others, so set this one only on projects that support it.

questions.question: A spec file has `test.use({ ...devices['iPhone 15'] })` at the top level. Where do its tests run?
options: In each project's own browser, at iPhone size
Only in projects named after an iPhone
Nowhere, because `test.use()` can't take a device
On WebKit, in every project
questions.explanation: A device descriptor includes its browser engine, so the file overrides the project's browser and runs on WebKit each time.

questions.question: A known Firefox bug breaks a test that can still run to the end. Which annotation tells you when the bug is fixed?
options: `test.skip(browserName === 'firefox', 'bug 123')`
`test.fixme(browserName === 'firefox', 'bug 123')`
`test.fail(browserName === 'firefox', 'bug 123')`
`test.slow(browserName === 'firefox', 'bug 123')`
questions.explanation: `test.fail()` runs the test and expects it to fail, so the run reports an error as soon as the test starts passing. Skipped tests never run.
